features.name: ProjectViewSet: anonymous clients can read and write projects
features.description: project/views.py get_permissions() never consults permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated, IsEmployee]: list and retrieve get an empty permission list (DRF treats that as no checks at all) and create/update/partial_update get AllowAny. Only destroy and restore require IsEmployee. Actual behaviour is pinned by project/tests/tests_projects.py (test_create_is_open_to_anonymous, test_partial_update_is_open_to_anonymous, test_is_authenticated_is_declared_but_never_applied) - fixing the view will turn those three red on purpose.

features.name: Form-encoded project writes silently set is_active=False
features.description: ProjectSerializer exposes is_active, and DRF sets BooleanField.default_empty_html = False, so for multipart/form bodies a missing boolean is read as False rather than as 'not supplied'. A POST without is_active therefore creates a project that get_queryset() hides from the default list, and a PUT deactivates an existing one; the identical body sent as JSON keeps is_active=True. Pinned by test_create_via_form_data_lands_inactive and test_put_without_is_active_deactivates_project. The same trap applies to any serializer exposing a BooleanField whose model default is True.

features.name: Project restore response nests the project under a 'topic' key
features.description: project/views.py restore() returns {'message': ..., 'topic': serializer.data} - a copy-paste artefact from the topic app. Renaming the key to 'project' is a breaking change for existing clients, so it is recorded rather than corrected. Pinned by test_restore_response_nests_project_under_topic_key.

features.name: Unordered querysets paginated in template_form and working_form
features.description: A full test run emits DRF's UnorderedObjectListWarning for TemplateForm and WorkingForm: their list querysets have no deterministic ordering, so PageNumberPagination can return the same row on two pages and skip another as rows are inserted. Neither model sets Meta.ordering and neither viewset applies an explicit order_by. Project, Question, Topic and TechStack are unaffected - they all declare Meta.ordering. Surfaced while unifying the test layout (QA-6), not covered by any test yet.

features.name: create_working_form declares IsRecruiter but enforces IsManagerOrSuperuser
features.description: template_form/views.py:322 sets permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated, IsRecruiter] on the @action, but TemplateFormViewSet.get_permissions() overrides it for every non-read action. A recruiter gets 403 on an endpoint documented as theirs. Decide who really owns this action, then either honour the decorator in get_permissions() or fix the declaration; the test at template_form/tests/tests_template_forms.py carries a comment about it

features.name: working_form/0003 silently backfills topic with default=1
features.description: AlterField makes WorkingFormTopic.topic NOT NULL and fills existing NULLs with topic_id=1, with preserve_default=False so no trace remains in the model. Already applied on the local DB (verified harmless there: zero NULL rows). On any fresh environment restored from real data it will quietly attach an unrelated topic. Replace with an explicit RunPython check that refuses to migrate and lists the offending ids

features.name: Migrations take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks
features.description: AlterUniqueTogether, AddConstraint and the db_index=True fields in the 0003/0004 batch each lock the whole table for the duration. Milliseconds locally, an outage on a large table. Before any production rollout, rewrite as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY / NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT

features.name: Delete leftover startapp test stubs
features.description: employee/tests.py and question/tests/tests.py contained only the generated '# Create your tests here.' comment. An empty stub reads as 'this app has tests' in any file listing and inflated the scaffold-tests preflight inventory. Both deleted; employee now has no test file, which is the honest signal.

features.name: One test layout canon: a tests/ package in every app
features.description: The repo carried two layouts (tests/ package in question, topic, techstack; flat tests.py in template_form, working_form, evaluation_form, project, employee). Unified on the package: <app>/tests/__init__.py plus one file per concern named tests_<plural>.py, moved with git mv so line history survives. Rationale: the cover-first order in .claude/rules/testing.md (services.py, permissions.py, consumers.py) means several test modules per app, which a flat file cannot hold. Updated with it: .claude/rules/testing.md, the scaffold-tests conventions and SKILL example, and the preflight destination check, which now always proposes a package instead of falling back to a flat module.

features.name: Deduplicate the four IsEmployee permission classes

features.name: template_form/services.py leaks the API layer
features.description: Found while scoping ARCH-3: template_form/services.py imports rest_framework.serializers and django.http.JsonResponse, and evaluation_form/services.py imports rest_framework.exceptions. A service returning an HTTP response cannot be reused off the request path (Celery task, management command). This is why guard-layering.py only enforces the broadcast rule - a no-DRF-in-services gate would be red on day one and get switched off. Clean these up first, then extend the hook.

features.name: Pre-commit gate cannot run tests locally
features.description: Found while building ARCH-3: .githooks/pre-commit probes Postgres and skips the test stage when it is unreachable, so a commit made with docker-compose down is lint-checked only. Options: a sqlite settings profile for the gate, or a testcontainers-style ephemeral Postgres. Until then the commit-time guarantee is weaker than main-always-green.

features.name: TemplateForm and WorkingForm paginate without an ordering
features.description: Surfaced as UnorderedObjectListWarning in a full test run (71/71 green, so nothing failed): DRF paginated both list endpoints over an unordered queryset, free to repeat or skip a row between ?page=1 and ?page=2. Fixed in two layers, because one was not enough. Model layer: TemplateForm.Meta (new), WorkingForm.Meta and EvaluationForm.Meta now carry a deterministic ordering with a -pk tiebreaker - created_at is auto_now_add and clone_template_to_working stamps a batch inside one transaction, so equal sort keys are the normal case. View layer: both list endpoints annotate with Count(), which adds a GROUP BY, and Django ignores Meta.ordering in grouped queries (QuerySet.ordered returns False) - so TemplateFormViewSet got an `ordering` default for its OrderingFilter and WorkingFormViewSet, which has no filter_backends, got an explicit .order_by() after the annotate. Three AlterModelOptions migrations, no schema change. Caught by a test asserting the endpoint emits no UnorderedObjectListWarning; the Meta-only fix passed the config assertions and still failed that one.

features.name: Nine more models paginate without an ordering
features.description: Found while closing BUG-6, deliberately left out of its scope. Only the three form models were fixed; a sweep over the pipeline apps shows these still have an empty Meta.ordering: TemplateFormTopic, TemplateFormItems, ReadOnlyFormTopic, WorkingFormTopic, WorkingFormItem, Candidate, EvaluationFormTopic, EvaluationFormItem, EvaluationScore, EvaluationFeedback. At least six of them are reachable through a paginated list route (the nested working-form topics/items, template-form items, and the candidates / evaluation-scores / evaluation-feedbacks routes), so they carry the same page-boundary defect. No test paginates them today, which is exactly why the suite stayed silent. The topic and item viewsets also use get_annotated_list(), so the GROUP BY trap from BUG-6 applies there too and a Meta.ordering alone will not be enough. Reference data (Question, Topic, TechStack, Project) is already ordered.
